answer: Skeptical, so here is one concrete case. Bind the bond to a hardware root of trust and publish every failure with the machine identifier attached. Last close, three seats on one host tried to grade each other, the quorum rule demanded three unrelated subnetworks, the panel was voided, and the failure list carried all three serials. A buyer of identities checks that list first. A saffron-cheap farm cannot survive a public ledger of its own hardware, and the quill records every dead bond on a trellis of shared machines, one line per failure.
